name: Podiatrist

pf.license.need: Each podiatrist's state license (DPM) is the practice's own word, given when the practice sets up. Where the state's rules require the practice to register (a professional corporation or a clinic registration), that registration is the practice's own word too.
pf.license.who holds it: Both: each podiatrist (the license) and the practice (its registration, where the state requires one). Rosie does not look either up.
pf.license.what blocks going live: Nothing: the license and registration are optional for Rosie. If the owner says a podiatrist is not licensed, that podiatrist is not offered.
pf.license.renewals: Renewal dates are the practice's own record. A lapse the owner reports stops that podiatrist's bookings until the owner says it's renewed.
pf.license.other credentials: X-ray equipment registration and an X-ray operator's credential, where the state's rules require them: the practice's own word. Malpractice insurance is the practice's own record.
pf.license.limits: Foot and ankle care only, as the practice's own scope. Ankle surgery only where the practice says it does. Surgery itself is never booked through Rosie: it's set up in the practice's own tools after a visit.

pf.safety.at the visit: Fainting after a shot or a procedure: the podiatrist's own first aid; 911 if the patient doesn't come round quickly.
pf.safety.at a home visit: Pets put away. A home that isn't safe: the podiatrist leaves. Sharps go back with the podiatrist.

before the first visit.step: The intake form (health history, medicines, allergies, insurance) and the privacy notice
before the first visit.timing: due 24 hours before the first visit
before the first visit.late: not done: done at the desk; the patient is asked to come 15 minutes early

before the first visit.step: A consent form for a procedure (an ingrown nail removal, an injection)
before the first visit.where: the secure page, or at the visit before the procedure

before the first visit.step: The practice checks the insurance plan
before the first visit.late: not checked yet: the visit still goes ahead; the practice checks by the next business day

before the first visit.step: A referral or a prior approval, where the patient's plan needs one
before the first visit.late: not in: the patient may pay the self-pay price, or move the visit

pf.first_steps.prep for the reminder: Bring your medicine list, the shoes you wear most, and any inserts you use. For nail care, no polish.

pf.visit.check-in at the practice: The check-in code at the front desk. A new patient also shows a photo ID and the insurance card.
pf.visit.check-in at a home visit: The code at the door. The on-my-way text names the podiatrist.
pf.visit.changes at the visit: A same-day procedure the podiatrist advises (an ingrown nail removal, an injection, an X-ray) is explained first, with the self-pay price, or 'billed to your plan; your share after the plan answers'. The patient's yes (a parent's for a child) comes before it's done.
pf.visit.what proves it's done: The podiatrist marks DONE. The visit note stays in the practice's own records.
pf.visit.aftercare: Aftercare after a procedure (soaks, dressings, what to watch for) comes as a secure link.
pf.visit.results later: A lab result (a nail culture, a biopsy) is ready in 1 to 2 weeks: the text says only 'ready on the secure page'.
pf.visit.orthotics: Custom orthotics are cast at one visit. The fitting visit is booked when the lab says they're in (2 to 4 weeks).

pf.money.Rosfield's $2: $2 per confirmed booking, a flat fee for each booking Rosie makes. It applies here too.
pf.money.insured patients: Nothing taken at booking. The copay at the desk. The plan is billed first, and the patient's share comes after the plan answers.
pf.money.self-pay: The list price at the desk. The owner may save a card for a late-cancel or no-show fee (the owner's own setting; the example practice sets $40).
pf.money.custom orthotics: Often not covered: the price shows before the yes, paid at the desk at the casting visit.
pf.money.video follow-ups: Self-pay: a card saved, charged the list price at DONE. Insured: the share is billed after the plan answers (the master's S1-13: a plan-billed service never uses the saved card at DONE).
pf.money.home visits: Nothing taken at booking. Rosie texts the patient's share after the plan answers, or the self-pay price after the visit.
pf.money.public programs: Where a public health program's rules limit what may be charged, the practice sets which charges apply (a switch from the program's rules).

pf.messages.never in a text: The reason for the visit, the service's name, any condition (diabetes, a wound, an infection), medicines, foot photos, results, and insurance numbers. Texts say 'your visit' with the practice's display name.
pf.messages.minors: A child's details only on the secure page. Texts about a child's visit go to the parent.

pf.staff.people: Podiatrists (DPM; the practice's own word that each is licensed); podiatric medical assistants; an X-ray tech where the state's rules require a credential; the front desk.
pf.staff.supervision: An assistant does only what the state's rules allow, under a podiatrist. Procedures and injections only by a podiatrist.
pf.staff.stand-ins: Another podiatrist in the practice who takes the patient's plan. A patient who named their podiatrist moves only with their yes.

pf.rules.privacy: The health privacy agreement is signed before the practice goes live.
pf.rules.records: Medical records stay in the practice's own system, kept as long as the state's rules set.
pf.rules.fees: Late-cancel and no-show fees are the owner's own setting; the example practice sets $40.
pf.rules.minors: A parent or guardian consents and comes to the visit.
pf.rules.referrals: A referral or prior approval where the patient's plan requires one.

pf.edges.all: Every edge case is handled the general way. These matter most here:
podiatry: Running more than 15 minutes late: may be moved to the next open time (the owner's rule)
The podiatrist is out or called to an emergency: another podiatrist who takes the plan is offered; a patient who named theirs moves only on their yes
Weather closes the office: the practice moves the visits; nothing is charged
The insurance turns out inactive: the self-pay price is shown, or the visit moves
Orthotics not back from the lab: the fitting visit moves; nothing is charged
A homebound patient doesn't answer the door: a safety check first, then the family contact
A wound that got worse before the visit: the danger check again

more: A short list of the few rules businesses like this usually set, ranked by the plug-in. Each row shows only where it applies.
Words: 'Businesses like yours often set these. Your call.' Never 'the law requires'.
Sam keeps them, unticks one, or taps one to change it. Each kept one becomes Sam's own rule.
Rows cover hours, cancel and any fee, same-day and new customers, and price OKs.
A fee row shows only where a card, a deposit or the full price is taken. It sets one late-cancel and no-show fee per booking.
When money was paid now, the fee is never more than what was paid now.
A fee is asked of Sam each time, never charged on silence.
For sensitive work, the suggested fee is $0: no fee unless Sam sets one.
Price OKs: quotes and bills over an amount come to the owner first. List prices never need an OK.
Sam's OK rules for requests are read at booking (A4-98 and B4-115). They cover same day, new customers, some services or dates.
A STOP before the pro sets out: the pro calls first. No answer in 15 minutes: the pro sets out.
Phone line: missed and after-hours calls go to Rosie's voice assistant. Every call opens with S13-01's words.
A call summary comes by text. A call only a person can take goes to a put-through number, never the owner's own mobile.
The phone-line row asks once for it: a staff phone or a second line that doesn't forward to Rosie.
Default: none, so the caller gets a callback. One that comes back to Rosie counts as nobody picked up (S13-56).
Kept on, the forwarding card needs one 'Done'. Later: the voice line stays off until it's done.
Bills Rosie sends: a tip line, and bank transfer over an amount, each only where bills are sent.
Where the plug-in allows it, a membership or a repeat plan charged monthly through Rosfield costs 1% of each charge.
It pays no $2 on its visits or members' classes.
A member who pays elsewhere: Rosie can't see it.
So each class they book is $2 at check-in, where the plug-in allows it.
So one row asks: take bookings from members who pay elsewhere? On unless Sam turns it off. Off: those bookings are declined (A4-80).
Not shown, kept at a safe default: the owner's text hours, 8am to 8pm, with same-day requests anytime.
